utterances.text: And it's page 4 in the English, and I believe it's maybe the fourth page for you. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before we go to that, I'd like to ask one more follow-up question. Mr. Andan, you told us that nominally, formally, their immediate superior in Bijeljina at the time was the undersecretary for public security, Mr. Kljajic. How was that? Could you explain that to me or remind me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to explain. He comes from a different organisational unit. And I should specify one more thing. We did not request Mr. Kljajic to send us Dusko Malovic's unit to Bijeljina. No. We requested reinforcements because it was our assessment that the existing forces at the disposal of Mr. Davidovic, and that was a part of the unit that I had formed in Bijeljina from policemen, that this was insufficient to cover our needs in the field. So we requested Mr. Kljajic to send us reinforcement through the ministry and the minister. And then a few days later, Mr. Malovic arrived in Bijeljina with his unit. And of course it was only natural that according to the hierarchy, he should report to the undersecretary who was the most senior officer in the institution. So it doesn't mean that Mr. Malovic was transferred by the decision of the minister to the area of the security centre in Bijeljina. He was told to report to the undersecretary Kljajic. And then he would be issued assignments and tasks that he was supposed to carry out. So I couldn't be his superior because I was an inspector in the police. Mico Davidovic couldn't be his superior because he came from another country. Mr. Kljajic was the highest ranking officer in the police station at the moment. He was the undersecretary for public security. He was an employee of the Ministry of the Interior. So it is only logical that Mr. Kljajic was responsible and a superior to Mr. Malovic, who I arrived in Bijeljina at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's just that I'm a little bit confused, Mr. Andan, about where Mr. Kljajic was at that moment. You said he was the highest ranking officer in the police station at the moment. In Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was referring to Bijeljina. Absolutely. He was in Bijeljina. He was with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Andan, I have to find a -- follow up on something in your answer to be sure it's interpreted correctly. Page 47, line 15, it's translated as: "So it doesn't mean that Mr. Malovic was transferred by the decision of the minister to the area of the security centre in Bijeljina. He was told to report to the undersecretary Kljajic. And then he would be issued assignments ..." Who was he told by? Wasn't Mr. Stanisic the only one that could have sent him there and directed him to Kljajic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. When I said that, I meant to say that the minister did not issue a decision whereby he would be transferred to another organisational unit. There was no decision which would assign him from that point on to the security services in Bijeljina. He came from the seat of the ministry to Bijeljina. It can happen in two ways. One way is for the minister to issue a decision, remove him from the complement of the manpower of the ministry, and transfer him to Bijeljina. He is thereby put at the dispose of the security centre in Bijeljina. He reports to the chief and says, By the decision of the minister, I'm now transferred and assigned to Bijeljina. So that's one way. And the other way is what happened with Mr. Malovic. I didn't explicitly say that Mr. Stanisic ordered him to be transferred there. I said we asked Mr. Kljajic to send us assistance. He spoke to someone in the ministry, whether it was Mr. Stanisic or not, I don't know, but he did speak to somebody who was most probably on a higher position than himself. And after a few days, Dusko Malovic's unit appeared in Bijeljina. That's what I said, Mr. Hannis. Maybe it was a bit confusing for you, but I am trying to explain everything quite clearly. I was trying to explain the situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One more, Mr. Hannis, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, is part of the confusion in our minds perhaps the difference between the public security ... Mr. Kljajic is public security, yes? Undersecretary for public security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The centre is public security as well, the centre in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. It's a lower organisational unit in relation to the position that Kljajic held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess I need to ask a question following that up am.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's my understanding that the centre in Bijeljina, though, a CSB, is a centre for both public security and state security; right? The CSBs have both public and state security or national security components?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're right. The organisational structure was taken over from the pre-war structure. So the Security Services Centre headed by the chief also had within its structure the state security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could go back to the document that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the last page in B/C/S and page 6 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a letter apparently from Zeljko Tosic concerning personnel matters, and in his letter he says: "With the outbreak of war time operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, I joined the special platoon, the police in Sokolac, on 16 May 1992, regarding which I am in possession of a decision number" such and such. "The platoon itself operated within the cabinet of the minister."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, again I have to object, Your Honour. He's reading -- Mr. Hannis is reading from the document which has nothing to do with the witness. It's the statement by some third person. I don't think that's -- according to the -- the rulings in this case so far, it wasn't allowed to be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm reading it as a preface to asking him a question, and I think it's something we've done for a long time in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was about to say, I was waiting to hear the question, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but, Your Honours, he can -- Mr. Hannis can pose the question without the reading from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... ah, sorry, I -- yes, thanks. I take your point. Yes, Mr. Hannis, you remember that we would have settled this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- would have settled this some time ago, that in a case such as this, you don't read the document into the record. You invite the witness to read it and then ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see that first paragraph on that page, in the letter from Mr. Tosic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the Special Platoon Sokolac, Mr. Malovic's unit, was within the cabinet of the minister? You saw those payroll documents.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, I cannot comment on the issue whether it was like that or not. It is true that the document says that he was there. That's what this person says, that he was in a special unit attached to the cabinet. But I have no other document stating that such and such unit belonged to the cabinet of the minister of the interior. And I don't think I am a competent witness to confirm something about this. These are matters that I'm not entirely familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 4 of the English and page -- I believe it's page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's a document dated the 16th of May, 1992, which is a decision temporarily assigning Mr. Tosic. That appears to be the document that's referred to in paragraph 1 of his letter; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there's a difference. I don't see that this is in the office in the cabinet of the minister of the interior. The decision simply says that he is assigned to the Special Platoon of the Serb MUP in Sokolac. That's what it says here. So this is yet another document that does not contain the claim that this was a special unit attached to the cabinet of the minister of the interior. It is true that there is a signature of Mr. Stanisic, but look what it says here, "in the Special Platoon of the Serb MUP Sokolac."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree. I think it needs to be related and read with all the documents that come with it and the other documents concerning the special platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 65 ter 20146.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, perhaps the witness can take the phones off -- his ... Thank you. I do object, Your Honours. First of all, we claim that this document is not authentic. We challenge the authenticity of this document. If you look at the page 4 and the part which Mr. Hannis read on the record, despite my objection, it is abundantly clear that the document was typed and signed by one Tosic, Zeljko. There is a line added. Theres a line added by the handwriting which says "this unit was performing tasks under the cabinet of the minister." Now, not only was this added obviously by handwriting, but if you compare, Your Honours, Mr. Tosic writes in Latinic, his signature is Latin, and the entry in the document is Cyrillic, the handwriting is Cyrillic. So with all due respect, Your Honours, we do object that this document goes in, because despite all our previous objections concerning the fresh evidence and all that, it stays as well. But this, this is -- this document, obviously, we challenge the authenticity of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I may add something for the Court's information in terms of our MIF which is our internal document about where we got this document from. This a document received on the 30th of March, 2009, from Milorad Barasin. Mr. Barasin is the Prosecutor, the chief prosecutor, in the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The document itself, each of the three documents contain signatures, stamps, and seals, and they appear to all be referring to each other, so they do appear to be part of one package. The handwriting, Your Honour, I don't have an explanation for that, but I think you can see this is a request for some kind of relief about a personal matter. The handwriting, I suggest, is likely that of someone in the office dealing with the request and making their comment about whether it should be approved. But I say that's matter that should go to weight rather than admissibility of the document. I don't think there's a genuine contest presented to the authenticity at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do you have anything to say about what appears to us as the lack of nexus between this document and the witness who is on the stand in regard to what his answer has been, his testimony has been?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I agree, he doesn't know much about that, although he did see Mr. Tosic's names on the payroll slips, but we can all do the same. I can't do that, so perhaps I should file a bar table motion to seek to admit it, rather than try to admit it through him. But I ask him to comment in the event that he might know something about this one, but it appears, I think, Mr. Tosic is not one of the individuals for whom we had a photograph and so we don't have that link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the basis of what we have there is insufficient to admit this document through this witness, so we needn't even concern ourselves with the other aspect Mr. Zecevic has raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, I'll try and deal with it in another way later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one matter that raises a big concern with the Defence. I believe I heard Mr. Hannis talking about the bar table at this point. I don't believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I heard that and you heard that, but we needn't exercise our minds about that at this stage, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we take the break: Mr. Andan, could you ... Do we gather that the air conditioning is making you uncomfortable? Is there something that should be addressed during the break? Is it in this room or in the waiting room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they stepped up the air condition. It wasn't -- it wasn't so strong in the morning. And I do mind such strong air condition in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: There is -- we said day before yesterday, there has historically been a problem in this courtroom. And one of the things that we noticed before the first break is that there was insufficient air coming in. And apparently in an attempt to correct that, they've -- where the witness-stand is, you appear to be under a draft. So I'll see whether during the break the Court Officers can make the necessary inquiries so that everybody is at least comfortable. So we come back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is on his way in, we understand, Mr. Hannis, that you estimate you would be another 40 minutes or so with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's right, Your Honours. I thought I might be done before we took the break, but we had some extended discussions, so that's why I've run over into this session. But I'm certain I will be done before the end of the day, I'm hoping within about 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And Mr. Zecevic, you'll begin immediately, and how long do you think you would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I have perhaps 10 questions from this witness, at this point. I don't know how much ... depends what happens in the last session. So I assume one hour, roughly, but depends on the witness's answers, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'm going to move to the last topic I have with you, and it relates to your suspension and removal from the MUP. I want to show you first 65 ter 015D1. This is tab 109 of the Prosecution's list. Mr. Andan, you talked before about what you referred to as the Sword of Damocles hanging over your head in reference to a poker machine. You recognise the documents on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is this the note reflecting the authorisation you had from Cedo Kljajic to take out and use that poker machine that we've had a lot of talk about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And your signature on the right-hand side of the page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Whose on the left, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now, but he was in charge of the deposit storage at the Bijeljina SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me show you another one. 65 ter 178D1. Tab 224.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The one coming up now is apparently dated the 28th of August, 1992. It says you returned one Jollycard poker machine that had been issued to you on the 4th of July. Is that your signature on the left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on the right we see Milorad Lovre. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the man in charge of the deposit storage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the 28th of July -- 28th of August, 1992, was this done after you had had the conversation with Mr. Kovac when he told you you weren't needed anymore?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I'd like to show you 65 ter 024D1, tab 214.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There are three pages to this exhibit. The first one is dated the 19th of August signed by Cedo Kljajic about sending a bus and a driver for the needs of the special unit. Was this related to the planned operation in Foca that you told us you were going to head up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we can go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is also dated the 19th, signed by Mr. Stanisic, it appears. Addressed to the Serbian MUP and the Montenegro MUP requesting permission for travel through the territory of Serbia and Montenegro on 21 August. This, too, was part of the planned operation in Foca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the last one in this exhibit is also dated the 19th of August, apparently has the signature of the undersecretary of national security, Dragan Kijac, scheduling a working meeting on the 20th of August. This also relates to that Foca operation that you were going to lead; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Only the name is not "Kijac"; it is "Kijac." And this is not his signature. Somebody signed on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I note, Your Honours, on page 57/21, the witness's answer was not recorded after Mr. Hannis's question that ends on 57/21. The witness's answer was not recorded. I think he confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Andan, I had asked you if that document by Mico Stanisic to Serbia and to Montenegro was part of the Foca operation and I thought I heard you say yes, but it wasn't recorded in the transcript. Can you confirm that you did answer in the affirmative?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I understand this last one you were looking at does appear to have signed for Mr. Kijac by someone else, but does a working meeting refer to the operation you were going to lead up going to Foca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I forgot if you told us, how many men were going to be in this special unit that was going to Foca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's leave aside this special aspect. It was a unit composed of workers of the CSB Bijeljina, and I think that it may have had up to 30 police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from the intelligence you had, how many people were you going to be trying to arrest or deal with in Foca? How big a group was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the intelligence we had, the information that the MUP had, 15 to 20 people were rampaging in Foca. There may have been some additional people, but these 15 to 20 men were led by a certain Pedo or Pedolino, whatever his nickname was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, we understand from your evidence that this didn't happen, you didn't go to Foca. Was that because you decided not to go? Or was it because permission from Serbia and Montenegro to travel through their territory didn't come through? Or why did it not happen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already answered this question. I said that as far as I can remember, we received a written reply from the Serbian MUP stating that they did not approve of our passage through their territory in this formation, whereas a reply from the Montenegrin MUP never arrived. So there was no way we could have gone to Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you also told us that you received some information from Mr. Davidovic that there was some sort of plan to ambush your group and kill you; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you learned that information, did you -- did you go see Mr. Stanisic about that or talk to Mr. Kovac or Mr. Kljajic or anybody in the RS MUP about that intelligence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was a discussion not with Kovac and not with Stanisic but I talked to Kljajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you say Kijac or Kljajic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kljajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what did you tell him about that? Did you ask him questions or just inform him of what you heard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that, Mr. Hannis. There was a dispatch from the federal SUP and Mr. Kljajic was familiar with it. He also knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was it after that dispatch that Mr. Kovac told you you were no longer needed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to show you an exhibit, P1269. This is tab 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I don't know if you will have seen this one before. It's the record of a meeting of the Collegium of the MUP on the 9th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a chance to see this because I wasn't a Collegium member.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. I didn't know if you might have been shown it at any time during proofing or one of your interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to go to page 6 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S on your screen, Mr. Andan, we need to go to page 3. At the very bottom of the page in B/C/S and near the middle of the English, there's an entry that says: "It was concluded that the following be carried out as part of the discussion of personnel issues: "1. Dragan Andan temporarily suspended for illegal use of poker machines discovered by the Working Group which had been appointed by the minister." Do you know anything about that? It appears my English translation says poker machines in the plural. Do you know what this Working Group was and what that's referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about the Working Group or its conclusion. If they consider that a Working Group, all right, but I considered them to be a commission that audited the hand-over that I performed before my -- before leaving the ministry, and it was headed by Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I know dates aren't your strong point, but please keep in mind for the next few minutes that this meeting was on the 9th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But before I go to another document, could we go to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, at the very top of this page we see "number 2, Danilo Vukovic, temporarily suspended for unbecoming behaviour and reckless endangerment." Is this the Danilo Vukovic who had originally gone out with you to Brcko and Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same Danilo Vukovic. And I know why he was suspended. If you want me, I can say why.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't at the moment. I'm trying to hurry and finish with you. But maybe I'm come back to it. I want to show you next 65 ter 031D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I'm not sure what tab this is, Your Honour, because this was not originally on my list. This one and the next one, 030D1, were two that I notified the Defence and the Trial Chambers by e-mail that I wished to use with the witness. It only came up during his last day of direct testimony. And I sent e-mails -- or Mr. Smith, for me, sent e-mails to the Defence and to the Legal Officers, I think, indicating that I wanted to use these two documents. So I don't have a tab number for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, have you ever seen this document before? It's dated the 11th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never received this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's entitled "Decision," and it says "Dragan Andan is hereby temporarily suspended as of the 11th of September." It gives a statement of reasons and it has the partial signature that appears to be Mico Stanisic's. I know you testified earlier in the week that you never saw any written documents relating to your suspension, so -- and looking at it now, that doesn't refresh your memory about whether you ever had a written document about your suspension? Because we see on the bottom left it says "send to above-named person," so it appears you should have received a copy.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why isn't it circled? Because that was the practice. When the above-named person received a copy, then the number would be circled, and we see it isn't. So I stand by what I said; I never received this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In terms of the disciplinary proceedings and the rules that were in effect at the time, was the minister of the interior able to initiate disciplinary proceedings, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to explain yesterday, but I can do it again. Of course he could, he had the authority to instigate disciplinary proceedings against anybody in the MUP, but in my case it wasn't necessary for the minister to do so. The chief of my organisational unit, and that is the chief of the police administration, Mr. Kovac, was the one whose duty it was. And I can repeat that Mr. Kovac shifted this to the minister in an insidious manner, without real need. Why he did so, I don't know. But there was no need for him to pass this decision on to the minister, because my chief of administration was perfectly able to do that himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Under "Statement of Reasons" you'll see it says "in his request number 09/2511 of 11 September" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the witness explained on at least three times that he never received the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But I'm asking this question to ask a question about the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but do please ask the question and don't cite the document which he never saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you saying this is not an authentic document? Your Honours, this is a document that was placed in the e-court by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think Mr. Zecevic's point is that the witness says he didn't receive it, so that the -- I don't know exactly what your question is going to be, of course, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll try and ask it a different way, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This document says that the reason for this decision is because the minister of the interior had filed a request for disciplinary proceedings. So in effect doesn't that mean that Mr. Stanisic is deciding on a request that Mr. Stanisic himself made; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I understood you, but I have already tried to answer. Maybe it isn't fully clear to you, but the minister can launch disciplinary proceedings and suspend any employee in the MUP. That's part of his legal authority. He was probably misinformed by somebody about the whole situation. Where, how, I don't know. But my question again is, why didn't Kovac do it? He talked to me, and you see that the decision is dated September 11th, but it doesn't mention that I requested a meeting with Mr. Kovac and said to him what I said. I hope I don't have to repeat. And it says here that I can appeal this decision within 15 days, but how do I do that? I never received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, what I understand Mr. Hannis's question to be, and indeed it is something that struck me when I looked at the document, is whether as a matter of the usual procedure it is possible for the minister to both initiate the request and to make the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that was procedurally possible. But I must return to my first point. I don't want to go into the subsequent procedure, but I did try to explain. Why didn't Mr. Kovac do that? because I was his subordinate. Why did he shift it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, we understand what you've said about that. Yes, Mr. Hannis, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Andan, Judge Hall made the point I was trying to get to, is that in effect it appears that Mr. Stanisic was acting both as the prosecutor initiating the proceedings and as the judge who decided on the proceedings requested to be initiated. As for the appeal, if you had gotten notice of the appeal, to whom could you appeal a decision on discipline by the minister? Who could you appeal to, do you know, under the rules?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did adopt this decision about my suspension and a decision about the initiation of disciplinary proceedings, but he is not a judge. There is a disciplinary judge, or, rather, a disciplinary body that consists of a number of people. This should have been forwarded to some other people as well, that is, the disciplinary judge and to the chief of my organisational unit for him to know that I'm suspended. The chief of my organisational unit tells me to leave the secretariat without a piece of paper of any kind and then I see this decision here. I could have appealed to the one who issued this decision. As some sort of a small-time lawyer, maybe that's how I understand it. But I can appeal to the minister and state my reasons. However, once the disciplinary proceedings are underway, they are conducted by the disciplinary judge and, well, what the final outcome would have been, of course, is something I cannot know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go to a related document. 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Unless I'm wrong, you were talking about two documents here, and we only saw one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm going to the second one right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, this is number 09-25-11, also dated the 11th of September, also signed by Mr. Stanisic apparently, and it's stamped. This is the request to initiate proceedings against you. Now, the question I have - under "statement of reasons" it talks about you having requisitioned a gambling machine, and under evidence it says "Dragan Andan" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm sorry, I have to object. The first question, I believe the proper question, would be to ask the witness if he received this document again. And if he didn't receive, then you shouldn't cite the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, have you seen this document before today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. And I would like to see Mr. Stanisic's signature if he's the one who filed this request. Is this document signed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the bottom the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you see the stamp and the signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I never received this document, and this is the first time I see it. I'm asking because I have a document that I was able to obtain but it was not signed by Mr. Stanisic or stamped.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this document and the last one we looked at, neither one of them was shown to you during your proofing with Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not. I do apologise to Mr. Zecevic as well, but, no, this has not been shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you -- you told us before that, I think, you didn't speak to Mr. Stanisic in 1992 after the last time you spoke with him at Bosanska Vila in Belgrade in August, before the would-be Foca operation; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think that is correct. And I think that I talked to Mr. Stanisic the next time in 1994 at the Kikinda building in Pale. I said yesterday -- well, perhaps my wording was too strong yesterday when I said that I was angry at Mr. Stanisic. It's not that I'm angry at Mr. Stanisic, but I haven't forgiven him either for not having found enough time to receive me and for me to explain what that was all about. And I did ask to be received by Mr. Stanisic through his secretary in Pale. I said yesterday that I received a variety of answers. Yes, we know, we'll call you back; leave your telephone number, the minister is on a trip; the minister is here; the minister is there. And that's how it went. After staying in Bijeljina for a month, I went to another organisational unit, that is to say, the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 1 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I know you told us that, but according to Mr. Stanisic on the document that's in front of you, you confessed to him on the 11th of September, apparently, in the presence of Dusko Malovic and Sinisa Karan; is that not true? You see where it says that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. This is not correct. You have Sinisa Karan. You can talk to him. And I claim with full responsibility that this was not the case. Mr. Stanisic is right here. So if court procedure allows him to do so, ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation or idea why Mr. Stanisic would sign a document that says something like this when it didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, this is even more than speculation, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, he may be in a position to know whether or not there's a motive for someone to falsify a document against him. The objection -- it goes to weight, but not whether he can render an opinion about who might have something in for him sufficient to cause them to forge a document, because that's what he's saying is that this is not a true document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm troubled by the question, but I suppose you have a point, Mr. Hannis. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Should I ask the question this way:

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, do you know anybody who would go to the trouble of trying to forge a document like this about you supposedly confessing on the gambling machines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot pretend to be a sorcerer, whether somebody would have done something or would not have done something. I told you yesterday, I had an open conflict with Mr. Kovac, but I still cannot say that Kovac wrote this up and planted it against me. I'm not going to pretend to be an old woman who is a sorceress here. I claim with full responsibility as a 60-year-old man that this is not correct. We have established all the facts, you are establishing all the facts, and I have never received either one of these decisions. Did someone do this on purpose so that I would leave the MUP as soon as possible? Obviously that was the case, because I was really bothering someone, wasn't I? When I say someone, I'm not referring to Mr. Stanisic. And if you ask me who that someone is, I'm going to tell you specifically who it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomislav Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You already told us before how I think some years ago, maybe 2005, Mr. Kovac made a written submission to the then minister of the interior alleging that you and Mico Davidovic had tried to kill him and other bad things; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I said that he made a written submission to the minister of the interior, but I did say that he filed a criminal report against me with the public prosecutor's office in Bijeljina. Perhaps you have some document in which he filed a submission to the minister of the interior, or some kind of complaint, but I did say before this Trial Chamber that he sent a criminal report to the prosecutor's office in Bijeljina, containing an allegation that I am trying to have him assassinated by the Zemun mafia that was on the run. That was it. I was interrogated about that and then I was given a decision on the cessation of the investigation involved, that is to say that there were no elements for conducting an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender these two documents, and I would also indicate, in terms of provenance, even though these were put into e-court by the Defence, they are OTP documents and the MIF information sheet says that these documents were received by one of our investigators from Mr. Tomo Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the witness never received these documents. They refer to him, but the witness specifically said that one of the documents contains untrue assertions. He confirmed, on question -- on question by Mr. Hannis, he confirmed who might be -- he didn't want to speculate, but he said there is a person who has the interest of that. Now we understand that that same person provided this document to the Office of the Prosecutor. It is on our 65 ter list, but it was put before we did have the opportunity to discuss -- to review that document and get the instructions from our client. Now, when I interviewed, proofed, Mr. Andan, he said he never received, so I didn't bother to show him these documents because he said he never received any document about his demotion or sacking from the MUP. That is the situation. And I don't see any basis for admitting this document to exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, you may think that we are about to put you on the spot - and you would not be incorrect - with that question I'm about to ask: For what purpose does the Prosecution seek to tender this as an exhibit? Is it for the purpose of the credibility of the witness or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, both, Your Honour, because I don't think you can make that ultimate decision yet, on the credibility of this witness, until you've heard more evidence about this. And also because it relates to what I say -- I should ask the witness to take his headphones off. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, could you remove your headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One of the Prosecution's view of this is that Mr. Andan was treated the way he was partly because he stepped on some toes by carrying out the actions he did, that certain members of the leadership in the political structure, as well as police and military, didn't like what Mr. Andan and Mr. Mico Davidovic were doing. And that's part of the reason he was dismissed. The poker machine seems a relatively minor reason to suspend this career policeman in light of what he'd done and what others didn't do. So that's part of the reason that I think it's importance to deal with this suspension. This is dated the 11th of September, but Mr. Andan was told by Mr. Kovac some days before that that he was out. So this just appears to be a formality to cover what was already being done in real life. And this is two days after the September 9th meeting of the collegium where he was on for being temporarily suspended on the agenda. So -- and I guess that's my argument for the moment. And also, I guess I did want to float one thing out to you in connection with this, is that under Rule 98, Your Honours have the authority to direct a party to call additional evidence, and you have authority to call witnesses on your own motion. And we suggest that Mr. Kovac may be a witness that you want to have called at some point before this case is over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must say, I'm a bit confused. Is this a motion by Mr. Hannis to re-open the case or a motion for rebuttal evidence? If either of this is the case, then it's not appropriate time, and we would like to be heard on that. And I still maintain my objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The evidence about these documents is that whereas the witness denies receipt of the documents, the documents are clearly about the witness and the -- sorry ... and about facts that he doesn't deny because there's clearly the background of some goings-on which culminated in his dismissal, and for that reason we allow the documents in as exhibits. So they may be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, therefore 65 ter 31D1 will become Exhibit P2348, and 65 ter 30D1 will become P2349. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I need to go back to Exhibit P2347. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you allow me one clarification question. Mr. Andan, you said, about the first of those two documents -- We can perhaps have it on the screen again, 31 -- 031D1. You said that you never received this document and then you add "I have a document that I was able to obtain, but it was not signed by Mr. Stanisic." Was that this document but without the signature? Something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You didn't understand me well then. May I say straightaway, I did not receive either one of these documents. Sometime in 2005, in the MUP archives, I found another document without Mr. Stanisic's signature. 2005. Just a moment, this is a decision on temporary suspension. I've never seen this. Never. As for the request to initiate disciplinary proceedings, I saw that in 2005 when I found it in the MUP archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So the request - that's the second document that was shown to you - you found that in the -- in the MUP archives, without the signature of Mr. Stanisic. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2005. In 2005 I found it. So the decision on suspension or the request on initiating disciplinary proceedings I have never received either one in 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995, never. I never received the decision or the request to initiate disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Andan. You never received it, it was never notified to you, but you found it in the archives in 2005 without Mr. Stanisic's signature; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second document. Not this document, but the other one. I have not found this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The second document in which it is stated that you confessed in the presence of two other persons to Mr. Stanisic what was said in the document, that's the document you find in the -- found in the archives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's right. I found it in 2005 in the MUP archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And I suppose that upset you at that moment, reading this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course it did upset me. However, it was all over and I could not have done anything retroactively. Enough time had elapsed to prevent me from doing anything about it. If you allow me, I will just say one more thing, please. Since it is my credibility that is at stake, I am going to present before this Trial Chamber just one thing that happened and that is true. I'm conveying a conversation between myself and Dragan Okuka, nicknamed Crni. The year is 2006. That's right, yes. When we talked in connection with what I had found in the archives, and that's what he said to me then. I quote: I went to a bakery in Bijela near Herceg-Novi that is owned by Tomo Kovac. Tomo brought me in to show me machines that bake bread and inter alia he showed me one of these machines and said, I bought this machine in Hungary and it cost me such and such amount of money. And I said to him, Tomo, why are you lying to me? You see that this is the machine that fell when we were stealing it from the state bakery in Rajlovac. Now you judge my credibility and his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I need to show you P2347 again. This is the Official Note by Bosa Darko Dodik from 12 December 2007, and I have a question. In the third paragraph on the first page, in the interview Dragan Andan said he'd been commander until such and such a date, that he was "forced out and that he had a decision on suspension from duties which he could show if necessary." What document were you referring to there in 2007? Is that some document different than these two we were looking at about discipline in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I meant to offer the document that I found in the MUP archives in 2005. That is the decision on initiating disciplinary proceedings. I've already said that it did not have a signature, but I can offer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to confirm that was the same one you were telling Judge Delvoie about. Do you have that document still, the one you found in the archives in 2005?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it at home. If necessary, I can send it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... would you be willing, after you go home --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Hannis, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you be willing, after you go home, to furnish a copy of that or the original of that to Victim/Witness or some representative of the Chambers so that they could have a look at it? Any problem with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no problem whatsoever. You are going to give me the address to which I should have this sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, before we go on, now I'm confused. I thought, before Judge Delvoie had asked the questions that he did, I thought we were talking about a third document. Judge Delvoie having -- by the time Judge Delvoie was finished, I thought it was settled that what he was talking about is another version of the second document that we saw that has been exhibited. Are we -- having regard to the witness's answer to your question, are we back to the possibility of a third document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it's the document regarding the request to initiate disciplinary proceedings, same as the one we have except without the signature of Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Andan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I suppose without the stamp or the seal as well; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right about that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Otherwise the typed stuff is all the same?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But that would remain to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do I understand the evidence to be at this point, Mr. Andan, that the document you have at home is, unlike the document that -- to which you testified earlier, one without a signature? Just concentrate on the signature question now. That is your evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hereby state that I have a decision on initiating disciplinary proceedings, that is, this document number 2, without a signature and without a seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So it seems to me that because it doesn't have a signature and a seal, once we have it in hand, a comparison's going to have to be made as to whether it's a third document or just a second version, different version, of the second document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I would request that the Trial Chamber, through the Registry, somehow make those arrangements so that it can be received. I would be happy to do it, but I think it's probably best to go through a neutral party rather than through the Defence or through me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the -- it is -- the Chamber orders VWS to contact the witness after he would have been released and returned to his home, and the -- to have the document sent on to the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, the last one I want to show you is 65 ter 1447.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's tab 313, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Andan, I know you've seen this one before. It's a newspaper interview of you by a woman named Sasa Bizic. My English translation says it's called "The Sting of the Yellow Wasp." And I understand when you were interviewed by the OTP in 2006, I believe in Banja Luka, you confirmed that the contents of this were accurate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an interview that I gave to Sasa Bizic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, and do you recall confirming to the OTP investigators who interviewed you in Banja Luka that you had read it and it was accurate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what I said, then that's it. I cannot remember what I said to him. Right now I cannot remember. But I'm expecting you to put a question and then I'll be in a position to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, depending on your answer to the question about whether it's accurate or not, I may not have any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I propose, Your Honours, because it's rather lengthy, that we recess for the day, I give him a copy to read, and then depending on what his answer is about whether it's accurate or whether he has any changes, then I may have no more questions in the morning, or I may have a few if he says something is not correct. And then I have nothing else. I don't know how best else to deal with the remaining 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, very well. That seems to be the most efficient way of dealing with matters. So we take the adjournment to -- and I think that you would have seen from the later schedule that we are back in this courtroom tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of June 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.31 p.m.,
